role: The second reading: each entry read to refute it, not to admire it.
method: Each fragment read whole beside what show.cjs prints for the grape (GRAPES, GRAPES_PLUS, TASTE, INTRO_GRAPES, GRID_SAY, GRID_READS, the service rows) and beside the Codex's region records for Rías Baixas, inland Galicia, Bierzo, Rueda, Rioja, Penedès, La Mancha, Jerez, the Canary Islands, Vinho Verde, the Douro and Roussillon.

Every fact the reviewed records do not already state was put to search: the label rules (Rías Baixas, Rueda, white Rioja), the histories (the rescue of Godello, the old golden wine of Rueda, the legend and the parent of Pedro Ximénez), the synonyms (Alvarinho, Gouveio and the name Verdelho, Viura and Macabeu, Listán Blanco, the Pedro Giménez of Argentina), where each grape grows abroad, and the service of Sherry.

The glass read as a blind taster would: each note asked whether a taster would nod, each prose field scanned by a script for a family word in disguise, each ladder set beside the Codex's own climate line for the place and beside the other five ladders of the chunk.

All six are home grapes, so there is no side by side to test: each home and abroad pair was read for a false or lazy generalisation and against TASTE.world (old for the three the Codex flags), and no question carries a worlds tag.

The four lines counted and said aloud for the five beats in order; the sale read for its two sentences and for whether it can be said to a guest; the cards and questions read for one key, four options of one kind and a stem that gives nothing away; the compare tells read from both sides against every fragment written so far that names these grapes.

codexRecords: The Rueda record (.scripts/regions/fragments/spain.1.json, shipped in js/regions/spain.json), its traps: Verdejo is not Verdelho; the Madeira grape is unrelated. The DNA summaries read give Verdejo as a cross of Savagnin and Castellana Blanca and Madeira's Verdelho as an offspring of Savagnin, which would make the two half siblings. The sources are secondary and rest on small marker sets, so the record is not shown to be wrong, but a different grape is the safer wording, and the table now says so for both Verdejo and Godello.

The Rueda record, its law: it teaches Rueda Verdejo and Rueda Sauvignon as label categories and plain Rueda as at least 50 per cent Verdejo. Reports of the revision of 2019 to 2020 say the two varietal categories were folded into one Rueda, that the half may be Verdejo or Sauvignon Blanc, and that a grape may be named at 85 per cent. The council's current specification (revision 4, May 2025) could not be opened from here. The table's wording holds under either reading; the owner may want the region record read against the specification.

js/data-grapes-plus.js, the Verdejo profile: its confuse line says Sauvignon Blanc shows pyrazine. The table says gooseberry and cut grass, as the brief asks of anything spoken. The author's flag, upheld.

js/data-grapes-plus.js, the Godello profile, and js/data-intro.js, the Albariño and Verdejo rows: each carries the bare word citrus, and the two rows white flowers and green herbs. Family words; the table names lemon zest, lime and grapefruit, honeysuckle and acacia blossom, fennel and bay leaf.

The Codex respells one name two ways in two places: PEH-droh in the service reference and PEH-dro in the Jerez record; pah-lo-MEE-no in the Jerez record beside the table's pah-loh-MEE-noh; go-DEH-yoh beside goh-DEH-yoh. The same sounds each time; only Macabeo differed in its stressed vowel, and it now agrees with the Penedès record.
The Codex's Penedès record calls Macabeo gentle in acidity and the Rioja council speaks of marked acidity. Both are right of their place; the table's structure line now says so.
unsettled: Whether Godello and Verdejo are kin to Madeira's Verdelho. A glossary reporting the DNA studies makes all three offspring of Savagnin; no primary paper was read. The table says a different grape, which holds either way.

How a La Mancha Verdejo differs in the glass from one of Rueda. Two searches found nothing. The warm rung reads ripe peach, melon rind and cut grass: the riper fruit is a taster's reading and the grass is the Codex's.

The Pedro Ximénez ladder. The grape has one climate and the schema asks for two rungs of two climates. The rungs now say that Jerez is hot too but damper, and carry only the fruit; a ladder of one rung would be the plain truth, if the spec agent ever allows one for a grape of one climate.
What the current Rueda rule asks of a wine that names no grape: half Verdejo, or half Verdejo or Sauvignon Blanc.

How the Rías Baixas rule for the Rosal and Condado do Tea labels is worded (70 per cent Albariño with the partner grape beside it, or 70 per cent of the pair together). The Codex teaches the second; the entry leans on neither.
Whether wines of Albariño made in Uruguay, California and New Zealand are mostly unoaked. Likely, and hedged.
Whether every source address still answers: none could be opened from this session.
settled: A wine labelled Rías Baixas Albariño is the grape alone, from any subzone; Val do Salnés is the coolest and wettest subzone.
Godello: the replanting project of Valdeorras began in 1974; Gouveio is the same vine and wore the name Verdelho in the Douro until a Portuguese order of 2000.
Gran Vino de Rueda asks for vines of at least 30 years and at most 6,500 kilograms a hectare; Dorado is aged in air and Pálido under flor.
White Rioja Gran Reserva: 48 months with 6 in cask, and the cask aged wine keeps bright acidity under its honey, hazelnut and beeswax.
Listán Blanco of the Canary Islands is Palomino Fino.
Sherry at the table: Fino and Manzanilla at 6 to 8 degrees Celsius, Amontillado, Oloroso and Pedro Ximénez at 12 to 14; an open Fino keeps about a week, an Oloroso four to six.
Pedro Ximénez: a parent is the old Arab table grape Gibi, the tale of the soldier from the Rhine is set aside, the vine is most likely Andalusian, and Argentina's Pedro Giménez is another grape.
Montilla-Moriles is hotter and drier than Jerez and ripens the grape further; its wines aged under flor commonly reach their strength with no added spirit.
